title: ROC, AUC, and a multiclass average
summary: What a threshold sweeps, what AUC ranks, and macro versus micro F1.

choices.text: An AUC above 0.5 means the model is calibrated: when it says 0.8, the event happens about 80% of the time.

Macro-F1 averages the per-class F1 scores without weighting by how common each class is, so a rare class counts as much as a common one. Micro-F1 pools the counts first and is dominated by frequent classes.
Raising the threshold on a fixed score usually raises recall and lowers the false positive rate, so a stricter threshold improves both numbers at once.
AUC is the probability that a random positive outranks a random negative. It compares models without picking one threshold, and a useless ranking scores about 0.5.
An ROC curve plots true positive rate against false positive rate as the decision threshold moves.
